title: Testing the Green
question: Before putting, are you allowed to test the putting green by rolling a ball or making the surface rough with your hand?

choices.text: Only rolling a ball is allowed
Only making the surface rough is allowed

explanation: You are not allowed to test the green by rolling a ball or roughening the surface. Doing so results in a two-stroke penalty.

juniorVersion.title: Can You Test the Putting Green?
juniorVersion.question: Before you putt, can you check the green by rolling a ball or rubbing your hand on the grass to make it rough?

choices.text: Yes, you can do both things
No, you can't do either thing
You can only roll a ball
You can only rub the grass

juniorVersion.explanation: You are not allowed to test the green by rolling a ball on it or rubbing your hand on the grass to see how it feels. These things are not allowed before you putt.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The smooth, short grass around the hole where you use your putter to try to get the ball in.
A soft hit (or stroke) on the green to try to get the ball in the hole.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Encourage children to look at the green to read it, but tell them not to touch it or roll a ball to test it before they putt.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think it is OK to roll a ball or touch the green to feel how fast or rough it is.
Kids may believe touching with a hand is not as bad as rolling a ball.
